transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-11
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lila Gomez (Redwood SE), Daniel Park (CTO, AegisPulse), Nora Hayes (Head of IT), Rajan Singh (Security Architect), Sofia Torres (Legal)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Maya, AE on the Redwood Inference team. Quick confirm who we've got on the call?
[00:12] Daniel Park: Hey Maya, Daniel here, CTO. Nora and Rajan and Sofia with me.
[00:18] Nora Hayes: Hi all.
[00:22] Maya Chen: Great. Today's goal — high level security posture discovery. We want to understand your compliance needs (SOC 2, ISO), SSO/SAML integration, RBAC, KMS/encryption, audit log retention, and whether Hosted, Dedicated, or Private fits. Ravi and Lila from engineering will cover the technical specifics. Sound good?
[00:37] Rajan Singh: Sounds good. We primarily care about data residency, encryption at rest and in transit, and whether keys can be customer managed — HSM if possible. Also SOC2 evidence.
[00:45] Lila Gomez: Perfect. We'll walk through each area and flag where there are configurable options or enterprise add-ons.

[02:10] Ravi Patel: Quick architecture primer — Redwood hosted is our managed API with multi-tenant control plane, we do tokenization, streaming, etc. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools for a customer — same runtime but isolated capacity. Private is VPC/private control plane, can be deployed in your cloud region or, with our on-prem package, air-gapped. Each has different tradeoffs for latency, cost, and control.
[02:42] Daniel Park: When you say on-prem package, is that a full runtime we run in our data center? Or do you ship some components to host?
[02:52] Ravi Patel: It's a customer-managed runtime — we provide the artifact and orchestration specs. For fully air-gapped deployments there's an additional engineering engagement; we can support HSM integrations and local KMS if you need to keep keys inside your network.

[05:05] Nora Hayes: On SOC2 — do you have the attestation and can we get a copy? Our procurement needs it for onboarding.
[05:14] Maya Chen: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II. I'll share the attestation and the summary page after the call. We also have ISO awareness and we can provide the security whitepaper.
[05:26] Sofia Torres: Do you also have the penetration test report redacted? We need a redacted report or summary of remediation.
[05:34] Maya Chen: We have a pen-test summary we can share. I'll include both SOC2 and pen-test summary in the follow-up.

[07:00] Rajan Singh: On SSO — we use SAML 2.0 primarily, want SCIM for provisioning. How mature is Redwood's SSO stack?
[07:09] Ravi Patel: We support SAML and OIDC out of the box. SCIM for user provisioning is supported for Enterprise customers; we can also do Just-In-Time provisioning depending on your IdP. There might be some small mapping work for groups and roles.
[07:28] Nora Hayes: Can you provide SAML metadata example and attribute mapping for RBAC?
[07:33] Lila Gomez: Yes, we'll send a SAML metadata sample and recommended attribute mappings (email, groups, role). Our RBAC model supports org/team/resource scopes and token-level policies — you can pin models, restrict endpoints, and set token read/write scopes.

[09:40] Daniel Park: Important: we need audit logs for any inference calls that touch PHI derivatives — retention for at least 7 years for our compliance. Can you retain logs that long?
[09:50] Ravi Patel: Default audit log retention for hosted is 90 days; we have add-ons for extended retention up to multi-year for enterprise accounts, retention is configurable and can be exported to your SIEM (S3/Cloud Storage or streaming to Kafka). For Dedicated and Private customers, you can control retention and storage destination.
[10:12] Rajan Singh: Export to our S3 with SSE-KMS? The logs must be encrypted with our keys.
[10:18] Lila Gomez: Yes, you can push logs to your S3. For Hosted we manage encryption, but we also support pushing encrypted logs to your buckets using your KMS. For Private deployments, you retain full control of encryption keys.

[12:00] Sofia Torres: Regarding KMS — do you support bringing your own key material (BYOK) or HSM-backed keys?
[12:07] Ravi Patel: We support BYOK through customer-managed KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS). For HSM, in Private deployments we can integrate with on-prem HSM or cloud HSM — there is an extra validation step and an engagement to meet FIPS levels. Hosted customers can use our managed keys or configure cross-account KMS for certain artifacts.
[12:31] Daniel Park: Is there a documented flow for key rotation and zero-downtime rewrap? We need to ensure rotation doesn't cause request failures.
[12:39] Lila Gomez: Yes, we provide a key rotation procedure; keys are versioned and there is a rewrap flow. For Dedicated/Private you can do staged rotation. We'll include the doc link in the follow-up.

[15:00] Rajan Singh: On RBAC — we want least-privilege. Can roles be scoped to model versions and to specific endpoints? For example dev team can call embeddings but not model-management APIs.
[15:12] Ravi Patel: Yes, RBAC is resource-aware: model actions (deploy, pin, rollback), runtime (inference tokens), telemetry access. You can create roles scoped to routes and models; tokens can be limited by time and by allowed model IDs. It's fairly granular.
[15:33] Daniel Park: Can we map our AD groups to Redwood roles via SCIM?
[15:38] Lila Gomez: That's the recommended approach — SCIM for provisioning and group mapping to Redwood roles. We'll show sample mappings.

[18:10] Nora Hayes: Data residency: we're regulated in EU and some data must not leave the EU. Does Redwood host in EU regions?
[18:20] Maya Chen: We have hosted endpoints in EU regions, and Dedicated capacity can be provisioned in specific cloud regions. For full control, Private deployment into your VPC in EU is possible. Our hosted service can be configured to keep data in-region but we recommend Dedicated or Private for strict residency requirements.
[18:36] Daniel Park: If we choose Hosted, is there any chance data leaves the region for failover?
[18:42] Ravi Patel: Within Hosted we try to keep paths region-local. For cross-region failover we can enforce policies; for strict regulatory requirements we recommend Dedicated or Private which guarantee data stays within your tenancy and region.

[21:00] Rajan Singh: About telemetry — what telemetry do you collect? Are prompts persisted? Can we opt out of prompt logging?
[21:10] Lila Gomez: We collect telemetry for performance and quality monitoring. For Hosted product by default we have short-lived logs and telemetry; we also offer options to disable logging of prompt content for compliance, especially for paid enterprise plans. For Dedicated/Private you have more control and can disable or route telemetry to your systems.
[21:33] Nora Hayes: We need a strict PII policy — is there redaction at ingest?
[21:38] Ravi Patel: We offer client-side redaction guidance and SDK hooks to redact sensitive fields before sending. We can help embed preprocessors as part of the integration.

[24:05] Daniel Park: Let's talk about latency SLOs — our product requires sub-200ms median for short inferences. What's realistic on Dedicated vs Hosted?
[24:16] Ravi Patel: For short sequences on Dedicated in EU region we regularly hit medians of 60–120ms depending on model size and batch config. Hosted medians are typically a bit higher due to multi-tenant routing, often 120–250ms. We'll share performance profiles for reference models and expected tail latencies.
[24:38] Daniel Park: Any isolation guarantees under load?
[24:42] Lila Gomez: Dedicated provides capacity isolation and configurable burst capacity; we also have model fallbacks and throttling policies so latency SLOs are more predictable.

[27:00] Rajan Singh: For on-prem, what's the upgrade path? We can't accept long outages.
[27:07] Ravi Patel: Upgrades are rolling; we support canary deployments and blue/green where possible. For air-gapped installs we perform a validated upgrade window with you. We also provide a rollback plan.
[27:25] Nora Hayes: Who signs the BAA or data processing addendum?
[27:28] Maya Chen: We have a standard DPA and BAA for healthcare customers; legal can send draft, and we can walk specific clauses with your legal team. Sofia, we can coordinate on that.
[27:40] Sofia Torres: Yes please, send the DPA. We might request a few edits around sub-processor lists and audit rights.

[30:00] Daniel Park: For logs and audit trail — how granular are the logs? We need user-level and request-level tracing including model version used and token counts.
[30:10] Lila Gomez: Audit logs include request metadata, user identity, model ID and version, response status, token usage metrics. We can correlate with traces for latency debugging. Logs can be exported to SIEM and we can provide sample log schemas.
[30:32] Rajan Singh: Are logs tamper-evident? We need to demonstrate immutability to auditors.
[30:37] Ravi Patel: We can support append-only logging and integration with WORM storage and signatures for immutability in the Dedicated/Private deployments. For Hosted we maintain internal protections and can provide attestations and export to your immutable store as part of the enterprise package.

[33:00] Nora Hayes: What's the support SLAs for security incidents?
[33:06] Maya Chen: We have an incident response runbook; enterprise customers get faster alerting and a named incident manager. SLA for security incident acknowledgement is within one hour for enterprise plus regular updates until resolution.
[33:20] Daniel Park: Do you share CVEs and vulnerability timelines?
[33:24] Ravi Patel: Yes, we publish advisories and maintain a security bulletin; we'll add AegisPulse to our notification list once onboarded.

[35:10] Rajan Singh: On encryption at rest for model weights — if we do Dedicated, are weights encrypted with our key?
[35:18] Lila Gomez: For Dedicated we can enable customer-managed key encryption for model artifacts in storage; in Private you're fully able to control encryption. In Hosted we use our managed keys but can support cross-account KMS where applicable.

[37:45] Daniel Park: Any surprises with export controls or restricted models? We're in regulated pharma contracts.
[37:53] Maya Chen: Some models have usage restrictions; we'll flag those in the model catalog. For regulated workloads, we recommend dedicated or private so you can pick vetted, quantized models and control inference paths.

[40:00] Nora Hayes: For the benchmark run — what do you need from us?
[40:06] Lila Gomez: A representative dataset (redacted if necessary), target request pattern, and test SLOs. We'll provision a dedicated slot and run the benchmark with monitoring. Expect about 2–3 hours of setup plus run time.
[40:20] Daniel Park: Can we use synthetic data that mimics our token distribution?
[40:24] Ravi Patel: Yes synthetic is fine — helps preserve PHI. We'll work with you on a dataset template.

[42:10] Sofia Torres: Contractually — we need an audit clause, termination data return, and a clause for data deletion verification.
[42:20] Maya Chen: Those are supported; we can include deletion verification and proof of deletion workflow in the DPA. We'll surface standard contract language and then iterate.

[45:00] Rajan Singh: Any known gaps? Where should we be cautious?
[45:07] Ravi Patel: The main gap for Hosted is absolute regional isolation and granular BYOK for every artifact — Hosted can support many controls but for the strictest regulatory constraints Dedicated or Private is usually required. Also, for air-gapped on-prem installs there is an engagement window and support overhead.
[45:26] Daniel Park: Makes sense. Cost will be a factor too, so please include mid and high estimates for Dedicated.

[47:50] Maya Chen: Quick recap of next steps: I'll send SOC2 and pen-test summary, Ravi will draft pricing/config for Dedicated, Lila will schedule bench run, and legal will share DPA. Anything else to add?
[48:03] Rajan Singh: Please include sample SAML metadata and SCIM mapping.
[48:07] Nora Hayes: Also include log schema and retention options.
[48:10] Sofia Torres: Add the DPA and subprocessor list early if you can.

[50:00] Maya Chen: Great — thanks all. We'll follow up by email with the docs and proposed times for the benchmark. Appreciate the thoroughness.
[50:10] Daniel Park: Thanks everyone.
[50:12] Nora Hayes: Thanks.
[50:14] (call ends)

Post-call notes: action items captured above. Transcription has some mis-hears (SAML sometimes transcribed as SAM-L, KV cache as K-V cash), cleaned minimally to preserve verbatim speech.
